sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Contextual Genesis**: Established by the Interim Government of India to examine the **Press Laws** that were historically used to suppress the nationalist movement.
• **Primary Objective**: To recommend the repeal or modification of laws that were inconsistent with the **Fundamental Rights** enshrined in the draft Constitution.
• **Core Mandate**: To ensure the press functions as a 'Fourth Estate' in a democracy while balancing national security and public order.
• **Key Metric**: The transition from 'Colonial Control' (pre-1947) to 'Constitutional Regulation' (post-1947).

items.definition: The government formed in 1946 that initiated the committee to dismantle the repressive apparatus of the British Raj.
A collection of statutes including the Indian Press (Emergency Powers) Act, 1931, which the committee sought to reform.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Legislative Review**: Systematic audit of colonial-era statutes.
• **Democratic Alignment**: Ensuring press laws do not violate the nascent constitutional framework.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Balancing state security with absolute freedom of the press.
• **Solutions**: Led to the eventual appointment of the First Press Commission (1952-54).

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'PIC-47' (Press Inquiry Committee 1947).
• **Decoded Meaning**: P (Post-Independence), I (Inquiry into colonial laws), C (Constitutional alignment).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Do not confuse the 1947 Press Inquiry Committee with the 1952-54 Press Commission. The 1947 committee was an immediate post-independence review, whereas the 1952 commission was a comprehensive statutory body.
Mains Value Addition: Use the phrase 'From Colonial Suppression to Constitutional Expression' to describe the trajectory of Indian press laws.

keyTakeaways: The 1947 Committee was the first step in decolonizing Indian media laws.
It focused on repealing laws that restricted freedom of speech without reasonable constitutional justification.
It set the stage for the First Press Commission (1952) which eventually led to the Press Council of India.
